skill.displayName: Pet Drying Box Heat Stress Analysis | 宠物烘干箱内热应激预警

version.changelog:
- Updated SKILL.md with version, description, and possible content improvements.
- Removed redundant or obsolete file: skill-card.md.
- No changes to code or algorithms; documentation only.

llm.summary: This skill does perform cloud video analysis, but it also silently creates or reuses an identity, registers/logs in with a remote service, and stores tokens locally without clear user-facing control.

dimensions.detail: Reading a user-provided local video and sending it to server-side analysis is purpose-aligned, but the artifacts do not clearly surface privacy, destination, retention, or consent details for local uploads, remote URL fetching, or cloud report history.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: No installer, scheduled task, or remote code download was found; dependencies are ordinary Python packages, but runtime initialization can create configuration/data files and a SQLite database.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill instructions require cloud history lookup and automatic internal identity handling while telling the agent not to ask for or expose identity values; this removes meaningful user control over account linkage and report identity selection.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The common utilities create a workspace data directory, persist a default user, store token and open_token fields in SQLite, read data/smyx-api-key.txt, and can silently call /sys/phoneLogin with register=1 and silent=1.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated pet heat-stress video analysis purpose is coherent with uploading a user-selected video or URL to a backend API, but the implementation also performs hidden identity bootstrapping, remote login/registration, token storage, and cloud report lookup that are broader than the visible analysis workflow.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable with pet videos or video URLs being sent to lifeemergence.com services, cloud report history being tied to an automatically managed identity, and local storage of account tokens in the workspace data directory. Avoid sensitive footage unless the publisher clarifies consent, retention, account creation, and deletion controls.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: The scanner concern is supported in part: cloud API use is expected, but hidden persistent identities, token reuse, and silent remote account bootstrap are not clearly disclosed or bounded by the pet-analysis purpose.
[YR4] unexpected: The YARA evidence appears to be a metadata/zero-width-character match in the description, and I did not find offensive tooling or exploit behavior tied to that finding.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The auto-login/register flow, generic HTTP/CRUD wrappers, and username lookup are broader than the declared video analysis workflow and increase account/data access surface.
[LP3] expected: File and network access are needed for this cloud analysis skill, but the artifacts do not provide tight user-facing permission boundaries or endpoint/file-scope constraints.
[SQP-2] expected: Sending supplied videos or URLs to backend analysis is expected, but the lack of explicit consent/disclosure for local media upload, cloud history lookup, identity handling, and local database creation remains a material transparency concern.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The advertised API options are partly unused, while common account persistence and identity storage are present; this creates a mismatch between the apparent user controls and actual runtime behavior.
[P9] unexpected: The whitespace matches inspected were formatting/alignment around wrapped expressions; I did not find hidden instructions there, so this finding is downgraded.
[E1] unexpected: External transmission of openId/mobile/source to the health-service login endpoint is artifact-backed and is not clearly necessary or disclosed for a pet video analysis user action.
[SQP-3] expected: Chinese-first user-facing text is visible and may be a usability limitation, but it is not a primary security driver for this verdict.
